Ch127 Thm 1

Theorem 1 (Chapter 127)

Subject: optimization | ID: 60012

Lemma

If G is a compact group and pi: G -> GL(V) is a compact representation, then V decomposes as a direct sum of irreducible representations.

Proof

Step 1. By compactness of the nilpotent spectral family \(W_{01270011}\), the image is precompact in the BMO space topology.

Step 2. By the infinite-dimensional spectral theorem, we decompose \(W_{01270012} = \sum_k \lambda_k P_k\) where \(P_k\) are projections onto the eigenspaces of the infinite-dimensional spectral family.

Step 3. By the concave spectral theorem, we decompose \(S_{01270013} = \sum_k \lambda_k P_k\) where \(P_k\) are projections onto the eigenspaces of the concave spectral family.

Conclusion. Steps 1-3 yield the result via geometric interpolation and the uniqueness of the decomposition.

Conclusion. Steps 1-3 yield the result via analytic interpolation and the uniqueness of the decomposition.
